correctness.rationale: For finite g_s, relatively free algebra equals coordinate-generated term-function algebra on g_s^n. Every bracket term is linear in ideal inputs u_i; polynomially varying action is P(a_i J_s) on J_s(a_i u_j-a_j u_i). The ring B_s=F_q[J_s]=F_q[eta]/(eta^s) is dimension s and faithful on the ideal. For nonzero a, some a_i !=0 makes polynomial evaluation onto B_s. Its kernel has radical the distinct rational point maximal ideal m_a, so CRT interpolates all nonzero fibers independently even when s>q. Basic scalar syzygies form a free B_s-module of rank n-1 at each a !=0, zero at a=0, yielding derived dimension s(n-1)(q^n-1); n independent t-coordinate functions give full formula, including n=1. Identity follows (aJ_s)^q-aJ_s=-aN_s(1-N_s^(q-1)), exact nilpotency index s for nonzero a; it fails for s+1 using top Jordan vector. Thus strict varieties and exponent q. Reconstructed a **separate** GF(2) term-function Lie-bracket closure algorithm: ranks (s,n)=(1,2)->5,(2,2)->8,(3,2)->11,(2,3)->31, agreeing with theorem; not an all-field proof.
